hi Patrick,
 (1)  No, you cannot fit a removal design with the colext function. I think you need to use PRESENCE or one of the BUGS engines for that. This is not hard to do, just that we don't have anyone working on the occupancy functions in unmarked right now so its unlikely to get done anytime soon.
 (2) You can't do that either with colext.
 
BTW, we're always looking for good R programmers that want to take the lead on some of this.
 
regards,
andy


 
On Tue, Aug 21, 2012 at 6:54 PM, pskolar <patric...@boisestate.edu> wrote:

Hello Group,

 

I am trying to analyze factors that influence occupancy of breeding hawks (habitat, disturbance, etc.) over two successive seasons.  I delineated potential breeding sites with a grid and I surveyed each site (grid cell) 1-3 times each season using a removal design (i.e. once a nest is located, the site has been determined to be occupied).  I have two questions about multi-season analysis and haven’t been able to find the answers to in previous posts or in any examples. 

 

1) Can a removal design be implemented with the colext function?  It appears that the data frame for colext is constructed by unmarkedMultiFrame which does not allow “type=removal.” Only unmarkedFrameGMM allows type to be specified, but I don’t believe a generalized multinomial-mixture model is right for my data or the inferences I am trying to make.

 

2) I would like to test if occupancy of sites was constant (Psi (.) p (.)) by constraining colonization and extinction probabilities equal to 0, or if occupancy was constant with changes in extinction and colonization resulting in population equilibrium (Psi (.) eps (.) p (.)) by imposing a constraint that gam = 1-eps or eps = 1-gam (MacKenzie et al. 2006 p. 206-210).  My question is how do I go about coding these constraints?

 

Thanks for the help
